newsitem.title: CANADA: Canada's Martin to look into jobless premia advice.
newsitem.headline: Canada's Martin to look into jobless premia advice.

text.p: Canadian Finance Minister Paul Martin said on Tuesday he would consider a senior government bureaucrat's advice to let the surplus in the unemployment insurance keep growing well beyond its current level.

Martin told reporters after a cabinet meeting that the recommendation was by Michel Bedard, chief actuary for the federal Human Resources Development Department, which runs the unemployment insurance system.
He said Bedard recommended letting the surplus in the fund swell to C$10 billion to C$15 billion and that he would consider Bedard's recommendations.

"I certainly accept the opinions of experts," Martin said in French. Politicians, including federal Conservative leader Jean Charest, have recommended immediate cuts in the premia. Charest said the fund would reach a surplus of C$5 billion this year and C$10 billion next year unless cuts were made.
The Financial Post reported on Tuesday that at least three provincial finance ministers said they would press Martin in an Ottawa meeting on Friday to commit to unemployment insurance reductions.
Annual surpluses in the fund go toward reducing the federal budget deficit. Martin said recently he would move as quickly as possible to reduce unemployment insurance premia, but gave no timeframe.
